episodes.title: Two Sides: One Nation, One Election
sources: High Level Committee on Simultaneous Elections, report (2024), as summarised by PIB (March 2024) and PRS Legislative Research, read 2026-11-16
Law Commission of India, 170th Report, Reform of the Electoral Laws (1999), section 7.2.2
Parliamentary Standing Committee on Personnel, Public Grievances, Law and Justice, 79th Report (2015), as reported by BOOM (4 Apr 2016)
J. S. Chhokar, Simultaneous Elections: Striking at the Roots of Parliamentary Democracy, The Hindu Centre and ADR, Issue Brief 8 (2018)
PRS, Bill Summary: Constitution (129th Amendment) Bill, 2024; News On AIR, 29 Jul 2026 (Joint Committee tenure extended to Winter Session 2026)

quiz.q: What did Arun say syncing all elections would require?
options: Cutting short or stretching some assemblies' terms
quiz.why: Bringing cycles in step means some assemblies' terms are shortened or extended, which critics say touches federalism.

quiz.q: In a Mains answer on this topic, what is the sound approach?
options: Pick the stronger side and argue only that
Both sides fairly, then a balanced way forward
quiz.why: The video's takeaway: set out both sides fairly, then suggest a balanced way forward.

quiz.q: Till which general election were polls mostly held together?
quiz.why: Simultaneous elections were by and large the norm till the fourth general election, 1967.

episodes.title: Two Sides: A Uniform Civil Code
sources: Constitution of India, Articles 25, 37, 44, 371A and the Sixth Schedule (Legislative Department text, read 2026-11-16)
Law Commission of India (21st), Consultation Paper on Reform of Family Law (31 Aug 2018), as reported by LiveLaw (31 Aug and 1 Sep 2018)
Mohd. Ahmed Khan v. Shah Bano Begum (Supreme Court, 1985), as quoted by the Centre for Law and Policy Research, UCC Part 2: Judicial History
News On AIR, 25 Mar 2026 (Gujarat UCC Bill passed; Uttarakhand 2024); Outlook, 2 Oct 2026 (assent; Scheduled Tribes exempt; Goa's 1867 code)

quiz.q: Why did Arun say Article 44 cannot simply be enforced?
options: It is a Directive Principle, not enforceable by courts
quiz.why: Directive Principles are not enforceable by any court (Article 37).

quiz.q: What did the Law Commission suggest in 2018 instead of a uniform code?
quiz.why: It proposed amending and codifying personal laws to remove discrimination; difference is not always discrimination.

quiz.q: Which article of the Constitution speaks of a uniform civil code?
quiz.why: Article 44: the State shall endeavour to secure a uniform civil code for citizens.

sources: Constitution (Seventy-third Amendment) Act, 1992, text inserting Part IX (Arts 243-243O) and the Eleventh Schedule, https://www.constitution.org/1-Constitution/cons/india/tamnd73.htm (read 2026-11-16)

PIB, New India Samachar, 16-30 April 2026, p. 38 (National Panchayati Raj Day), https://newindiasamachar.pib.gov.in/WriteReadData/flipbook/2026/Apr/2nd/English/files/basic-html/page38.html (read 2026-11-16)

quiz.q: Which committee's 1957 report led to the three-tier Panchayati Raj system?
quiz.why: The Balwant Rai Mehta committee recommended village, block and district bodies; Nagaur started the system in 1959.

quiz.q: Which Constitutional Amendment added Part IX on Panchayats?
quiz.why: The 73rd Amendment (1992, in force 24 April 1993) inserted Part IX and the Eleventh Schedule.

quiz.q: What is the minimum share of seats reserved for women in Panchayats?
quiz.why: Article 243D reserves not less than one-third of seats for women.

quiz.q: How were voters who could not read helped to choose in the first general election of 1951-52?
options: A separate box per candidate, marked with a symbol
A single box with colour-coded slips
Names read out aloud at the booth
quiz.why: Each candidate had a separate steel box at the booth, marked with the candidate's symbol.

quiz.q: When were EVMs first used across all 543 Lok Sabha constituencies?
quiz.why: EVMs were used in all 543 parliamentary constituencies in 2004.

quiz.q: What does VVPAT add to an EVM?
options: A printed slip the voter can see
quiz.why: VVPAT (rules amended in 2013) gives a paper trail: a printed slip shown to the voter.

episodes.title: The CAG: Parliament's Auditor
sources: Constitution of India, Articles 148-151, as reproduced on the CAG's site (Office of the Accountant General, Uttarakhand, Constitutional arrangement), https://cag.gov.in/ag/uttarakhand/en/page-ag-uttarakhand-constitutional-arrangement (read 2026-11-16)
Comptroller and Auditor-General's (Duties, Powers and Conditions of Service) Act, 1971, section 4, https://cag.gov.in/en/page-duties-power-and-conditions-of-services-act (read 2026-11-16)
CAG, Director General of Audit (Coal) Kolkata, Legislation Committees (PAC and COPU), https://cag.gov.in/mab/kolkata-ii/en/page-mab-kolkata-ii-legislation-committees (read 2026-11-16)

quiz.q: How is the CAG removed from office?
options: By a simple vote of the Lok Sabha
quiz.why: Article 148(1): removal in like manner and on like grounds as a Judge of the Supreme Court.

quiz.q: Where do the CAG's reports on the Union's accounts go first?
quiz.why: Article 151: Union reports go to the President, who has them laid before each House of Parliament.

quiz.q: What happens to the CAG's office after leaving it?
options: Cannot hold further office under the Government of India or a State
Must retire from public life for 20 years
quiz.why: Article 148(4) bars further office under the Union or any State after he ceases to hold office.

quiz.q: Which river is known as the Tsangpo in Tibet?
quiz.why: The Brahmaputra is the Tsangpo in Tibet, the Siang or Dihang as it enters India, and the Jamuna in Bangladesh.

quiz.q: Which three rivers went to India under the Indus Waters Treaty of 1960?
quiz.why: The eastern rivers, Ravi, Beas and Sutlej, went to India; the western rivers, Indus, Jhelum and Chenab, to Pakistan.

quiz.q: Where does the Ganga get its name, after the Bhagirathi meets the Alaknanda?
quiz.why: At Devprayag the Bhagirathi meets the Alaknanda and the river is called the Ganga from there.

sources: UNESCO World Heritage List, Aapravasi Ghat (entry 1227), https://whc.unesco.org/en/list/1227 (read 2026-11-19)

Girmit.org, History (Fiji): the Leonidas, 3 March to 14 May 1879, five-year contracts, origin of the word girmit, deaths on board, coolie lines, https://girmit.org/index.php/history/ (read 2026-11-19; community history site, secondary)
Scroll.in magazine, feature on the girmit, https://scroll.in/magazine/886645/scroll_in (read 2026-11-19; secondary): oral histories of the voyage, return-passage terms after five and ten years

quiz.q: In the video's diary, how many years does the girmit contract run?
quiz.why: The contract required five years of work in Fiji; return passage at the government's cost came only after ten.

quiz.q: The word 'girmit' comes from which English word?
quiz.why: Girmit is how Indian labourers said 'agreement'.

quiz.q: Which island received almost half a million indentured labourers between 1834 and 1920, and has a UNESCO site for it?
quiz.why: UNESCO's Aapravasi Ghat in Port Louis, Mauritius: almost half a million labourers arrived there, 1834 to 1920.

episodes.title: Quiz: The Anti-Defection Law
sources: Constitution of India, Tenth Schedule (paras 2, 3, 4, 6), text as reproduced at https://courtbook.in/constitution/schedule/tenth-schedule-provisions-as-to-disqualification-on-ground-of-defection (read 2026-11-19; reproduction of the official text)

Understand UPSC, Tenth Schedule / Anti-Defection Law, https://www.understandupsc.com/tenth-schedule-anti-defection-law/ (read 2026-11-19; secondary): 52nd Amendment 1985, 91st Amendment 2003, judicial review (Kihoto Hollohan, 1992)

quiz.q: Who decides whether a member is disqualified for defection?
quiz.why: Paragraph 6 of the Tenth Schedule refers the question to the Chairman or Speaker; courts can review the decision.

quiz.q: A merger protects members from disqualification only if how many of the legislature party agree?
quiz.why: Paragraph 4 recognises a merger only if at least two-thirds of the legislature party agree.

quiz.q: Which Amendment Act inserted the Tenth Schedule in 1985?
quiz.why: The 52nd Amendment Act, 1985 inserted it; the 91st (2003) later removed the one-third split.

quiz.q: Where was the Reserve Bank's gold sent in July 1991 as security for a loan?
options: To the Bank of England and the Bank of Japan
To the Federal Reserve in New York
To the World Bank in Washington
quiz.why: The RBI pledged 46.91 tonnes with the Bank of England and the Bank of Japan for about US$405 million.

quiz.q: In 1991 the rupee was devalued in how many steps, early in July?
quiz.why: In two steps, on 1 and 3 July 1991.

quiz.q: Which date in 1991 saw the new industrial policy and budget that loosened licensing?
quiz.why: The budget and the new industrial policy came on 24 July 1991.

quiz.q: What happened after the Kaira farmers' fifteen-day milk strike?
options: Their demand for a co-operative was accepted
Milk prices were fixed by contractors
The Bombay Milk Scheme was extended to Delhi
quiz.why: The milk commissioner of Bombay visited, assessed the situation and accepted the farmers' demand; the union was registered on 14 December 1946.

quiz.q: What was the bedrock of Operation Flood?
quiz.why: NDDB says the bedrock of Operation Flood has been village milk producers' co-operatives (the Anand pattern).

quiz.q: Which four cities did Phase I of Operation Flood link to milksheds?
quiz.why: Phase I (1970-80) linked 18 milksheds with Delhi, Mumbai, Kolkata and Chennai.
